subject: Intermittent request failures impacting AlphaTek — headroom mitigation
messages:
From: Jared Mills <jared@alphatek.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in empty/failed responses this morning

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

We're seeing intermittent empty responses (200 with empty body) and a handful of 502s from the Redwood hosted inference API since ~08:45 PT. It started for a subset of our production traffic (models:gpt-large) and is affecting our chat flow for a handful of customers.

Quick context:
- Region: us-west-1
- Estimated affected requests: ~0.5% of traffic in the last 20m
- Sample request IDs attached (alpha_error_log_20261020.txt)

Can you confirm if there is a known capacity/queueing event on your side? We rely on steady p95/99 latency for our SLA — this is starting to cascade into timeouts on our end.

Thanks,
Jared
Operations Lead, AlphaTek

Attachment: alpha_error_log_20261020.txt (text/plain)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jared Mills <jared@alphatek.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in empty/failed responses this morning

Hi Jared — thanks for the heads up and for sending the sample IDs. I'm escalating to infra and sending an initial customer-facing acknowledgement while we investigate.

What we're doing now:
- I've opened an incident and posted an initial note on our status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/2026-10-20-headroom-capacity
- Marissa, Laura, Ben — can infra confirm whether this is an emergence of prefix headroom/backpressure or a routing imbalance? If it's headroom, we may already have a short mitigation (soft cap on burst routing) to prevent empty payloads.
- Jared — we've got your logs; if you can capture one more trace with X-Request-ID in the next 30 mins that'd help (we pulled the attached).

I'll follow up with a targeted update in 30–45 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority.

—Rishi
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Developer-first LLM inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike in empty/failed responses this morning

Forwarding Jared's report and the sample log. Quick triage notes from infra side:

- Observed short-lived headroom pressure in us-west-1 starting 08:42–08:52 PT correlating with a burst from a batch of long-context init calls.
- Some routing decisions fell back to a thinner serving tier briefly; those fallbacks returned empty bodies in ~0.3% of traces (reproduction with same model variant is possible).
- Mitigation applied at 09:12 PT: increased headroom reservation for session affinity and applied a temporary backpressure throttle to bursty routes.

Action items for customer-facing comms:
1) Confirm we have Jared's exact request ids (done) and share a short remediation note.
2) Offer a short-term recommendation: pin to the more conservative model variant during the next 24h or enable our explicit burst protection toggle (we can flip it for them).
3) Promise a follow-up postmortem with timeline and root cause.

I'll prepare the technical write-up for the postmortem and coordinate with Laura on the status page follow-up.

—Marissa
Sr. Product Ops — Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jared Mills <jared@alphatek.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Update: Intermittent empty/failed responses — mitigation complete and next steps

Hi Jared — quick update now that infra has completed the initial remediation and we've scoped the follow-up: 

Summary of resolution:
- What happened: a short-lived headroom pressure event in our us-west-1 serving pool during a burst of long-context initialization calls caused a small percentage of routed requests to land on a thinner fallback path, which returned empty bodies for some model variants.
- When: 2026-10-20 08:42–09:12 PT (root cause window); mitigation applied at 09:12 PT.
- Customer impact: ~0.3–0.6% of requests for affected model variant in AlphaTek's traffic; visible as empty responses and occasional 502s.

What we did for AlphaTek:
- Immediately reserved additional headroom for session-affine routes in us-west-1 (temporary uplift).
- Applied targeted backpressure throttles for identified bursty routes to stabilize inference paths.
- Provided you an option to pin to the conservative model variant or to enable our burst-protection toggle (we proactively enabled burst-protection for your account for the next 24 hours; you can opt out).

Follow-up / Postmortem plan:
- We're preparing a full incident postmortem with timeline, root cause analysis, and long-term mitigations (kernel selection adjustments and routing heuristics). Expect that within 72 hours.
- I'll share the internal postmortem doc and the status page follow-up link once it's published: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/2026-10-20-headroom-capacity

Short-term recommendations for AlphaTek:
- Continue with the burst-protection toggle enabled for 24h; let us know if you'd prefer the pin-to-conservative option instead.
- If you see any further anomalies, include X-Request-ID trace and timestamp and reply here so we can correlate immediately.

Apologies again for the disruption — if you'd like a quick call to walk through the timeline, I'm available this afternoon or tomorrow morning.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0199
